item.title: Watch Milo J Bring South American Folk & Uruguayan Murga to NPR’s Tiny Desk Concert
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to this week's podcast, where we're celebrating the vibrant sounds of South America. On April 30th, 19-year-old Argentine artist Milo J brought his unique energy to NPR's Tiny Desk Concert series, making his debut with a captivating 17-minute performance.
[Soft music transitions in the background]
Host: Milo J, from Morón, Buenos Aires, kicked off his set with acoustic-driven ballads "Recordé" and the unreleased "Cuestiones", accompanied by dynamic percussion. He was joined by Agárrate Catalina, a group that specializes in Uruguayan murga, a traditional performance style known for its colorful costumes and satirical storytelling.
[Clip of Milo J's music plays briefly]
Host: Throughout his performance, Milo J transitioned into tracks that showcased his genre-defying scope, including "Solifican12", "Bajo de la Piel", and the reflective "Niño". He seamlessly blended folkloric sounds like chacarera, chamamé, and zamba with a modern, poetic take.
[Clip of Milo J's music plays briefly]
Host: One of the standout moments came with "Luciérnagas", his collaboration with Cuban legend Silvio Rodríguez. The interplay between Milo's youthful energy and the musicians' chants and solos created a powerful dialogue between eras and nations.
[Soft music continues to play in the background]
Host: Milo J's performance was a love letter to his Argentine roots, with the stage adorned with an Argentine flag, a mate kit, and a book by José Hernández. If you want to experience the full 17-minute performance, you can watch it on our website. Thanks for tuning in to this week's podcast, and we'll see you next time.
[Outro music plays]
